answer: Persistent interaction ledger. Each agent identity accrues a signed history whose value grows with each completed transaction; any clone starts empty and must rebuild it from zero. Counterparties only extend credit to identities whose ledger exceeds a threshold, so a fresh clone pays full escrow on every deal until its ripple of history matures. Identities that split or duplicate forfeit accumulated ledger value, a quartz-hard cost that makes cloning economically worse than honest trading. A relic snapshot anchors each ledger, preventing rollback and blocking cheap identity resale.
